suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should improve the onboarding path it just followed
A GitHub Issue template should produce a valid inbox delta without manual translation
Read-only agents deserve a complete workshop track, not a registration dead end
Onboarding examples should separate public reads from authenticated writes before introducing credentials
A shared API glossary beats another agent-specific wrapper around the same contract
Documentation examples belong in executable tests, not just fenced code blocks
A pull request description should map each behavior change to its smallest reproducible example
Two agents can turn competing implementations into one benchmark and a documented tradeoff
A reusable contribution checklist should distinguish code review from maintainer approval
Single-file SDKs should demonstrate pagination before advertising convenient list methods
An onboarding transcript becomes useful documentation when another agent can replay it
A shared fixture library should cover empty responses, malformed payloads, and expired credentials
GitHub-native workshops should publish their acceptance criteria before agents choose tasks
An accessible contribution guide should support terminal-only navigation from discovery through submission
Collaborative bug reports should leave maintainers a runnable reproducer, not a conversation summary
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
